solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Game where striker put on trial

indicators.note: put on says the striker word is placed after the trial word, as an addition

parts.note: a match is struck to light it, so it is a striker

explanation.surface: A footballer is tried out in a game to see whether they can score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' tells you the striker word goes after the trial word. A test match is an international cricket or rugby game.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is an international fixture, a kind of sporting game between national teams.

clue.text: Trained first of teaching assistants, yours truly

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: Someone who trained the first teaching assistants boasts that it was them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tame animal has been trained or domesticated, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: Fish I snared, all at sea

indicators.note: something all at sea is confused and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An angler boasts of catching a fish out on the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Soldiers in part of regiment

indicators.note: in part of says the answer is a piece sitting within the next word

parts.note: the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: Troops are stationed in one section of a regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Men is a standard collective word for ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers.

clue.text: String of invective from one in job

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the word for job

explanation.surface: A worker unleashes a stream of abuse while at their job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a sustained outpouring of abuse.

clue.text: Evergreen, white plant

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a plant with evergreen leaves and white flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' and 'white' look like adjectives describing the plant, but each is a noun in its own right; hock is a British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollyhock is a tall garden plant of the mallow family with spikes of flowers.

clue.text: Selfishly keep pig

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to keep something greedily to oneself
second meaning: a pig, especially one reared for slaughter

explanation.surface: Someone greedily hangs on to a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for greedy monopolising and a noun for a domestic swine.

clue.text: Possible Indian hiding in bush in Dunstable

indicators.note: hiding in says the answer is concealed within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of bush, all of in and the start of Dunstable

explanation.surface: Someone from India might be lurking in a shrub in Dunstable, a town in Bedfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu follows the main religion of India, so an Indian may well be one, hence 'possible'.

clue.text: Leader in government has moved to the slum area

indicators.note: letters that have moved are no longer in their original order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political leader has relocated to the poorest part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a deprived, crowded urban district, a slum quarter.

clue.text: Sailor runs into sea with little hesitation

indicators.note: into puts the abbreviation for runs inside the word for sea

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
er is the short sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A seaman hurries into the waves, barely pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea' as MAIN is an old poetic usage (the Spanish Main); the runs abbreviation comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariner is a literary word for a seaman or sailor.

clue.text: Pierce fine material, threading first of needles through

indicators.note: threading something into a fabric puts it inside that fabric
completes the threading image: the needle passes right inside the material

parts.note: lace is a delicate open fabric

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone sews delicate fabric, pushing a needle through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce or cut open, as a doctor does a boil.

clue.text: Nothing going on?

parts.note: surface reading: nothing is happening, all is quiet
setter's reading: not a stitch of clothing is being worn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Going on' suggests events, but read it as clothes being put on: with nothing on you are dressed as on the day you were born.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for nakedness jokingly calls bare skin the outfit you wore at birth.

clue.text: Tricky matter: ten for hospital care

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An awkward question of whether ten patients can get a hospital bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the medical care given to a patient in hospital.

clue.text: Fundraising event in Tenerife, terrible

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of Tenerife and the start of terrible

explanation.surface: A charity do held in Tenerife was dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair, typically held to raise money for a church or charity.

clue.text: Ostensibly round balls, spheres primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means taking what comes first, so the opening letters of the words are used

explanation.surface: Things that look round, balls and spheres above all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: its first four words open with the answer's letters, and the description fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbs are spherical objects, round balls or globes.

clue.text: Girl, one going after boy from South Asia

indicators.note: going after says the girl and one follow the word for boy

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl chases after a boy from South Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: a Bengali dish is one from South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali describes a person or thing from Bengal, a region of South Asia.

clue.text: Get boat out at home

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their usual places

explanation.surface: An instruction to take the boat out from where it is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get or acquire it.

clue.text: State of insensibility in chaotic US port

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is left dazed by a hectic American harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed condition in which a person is barely conscious.

clue.text: Wonderful, inspirational action?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: inspiration is drawing in air, so this is the act of inhaling

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspirational' looks like praise, but inspiration is also the technical word for breathing in; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something breathtaking is so astonishing it makes you gasp; literally the phrase describes inhaling.

clue.text: Former gesture, completely accurate

parts.note: an act, as in a gesture of goodwill

explanation.surface: A past gesture is recalled with complete precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise, correct in every detail.

clue.text: Light timber

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ray or shaft of light
second meaning: a long piece of squared wood in a building

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as lightweight wood, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a shaft of light and a structural length of timber.

clue.text: A wizard after Potter's head, fast

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter

parts.note: a wizard at something is an ace

explanation.surface: A wizard chases Harry Potter's head at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the wizard word behind the P. The wizard is not Harry: it means an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning quickly, so it matches fast used as an adverb.

clue.text: Stealing tablet, turn grey

definitions.note: a noun here, the act of theft

parts.note: to age is to grow old and turn grey

explanation.surface: Stealing pills makes a person go grey with worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillage is plundering, the violent theft of goods in war.

clue.text: Sign initials on line, entering office

indicators.note: initials are the first letters of words, so the next words give their openings

explanation.surface: An instruction to initial on the dotted line when taking up office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign initials' looks like one instruction; 'Sign' is the definition, a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Clear trap

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make as profit after deductions
second meaning: to catch, as in a mesh

explanation.walkthrough: To clear a sum is to earn it after costs, the financial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs the word means to make as clear profit and to catch something in a mesh.

clue.text: Fault is admitted by outsiders in team for bombings etc

definitions.note: the answer is the general name for such acts, not a plural

indicators.note: admitted by means let inside the letters that follow
the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of team

explanation.surface: A team of outsiders admits fault for a string of bombings.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrorism is violence such as bombings used to intimidate for political ends.
